page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor with an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a base speed of 2.55 GHz, utilizing 16 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, ensuring dedicated execution resources. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests ranking in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, and Passmark CPU metrics generally fall within the average range. However, memory bandwidth presents a notable performance tradeoff. While cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 1028.21 GB/sec, uncached large-block read bandwidth is weak at 23.77 GB/sec, and large-block write bandwidth is poor, falling into the bottom 10% at 12.96 GB/sec. This indicates that workloads heavily reliant on large-scale, uncached memory writes may experience bottlenecks.

Given its compute-heavy 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated physical cores, the ecs.c7a.4xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. It is well-suited for workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, text processing, and moderate database operations. It also demonstrates strong performance in text generation for small language models, making it viable for lightweight inference tasks.
